owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. Akien owns the bound already given and not CC's to widen: orient, then constrain, then survey, and the other four wait on these three WORKING (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap).

watchme.as_cast_verbatim: PROBE at cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/probes/ — and this one is not optional, because the whole ticket is an honesty claim about a number. It carries the derived floor fraction over berthed orient packets and is ENOUGH when that fraction is measured rather than declared, i.e. when no packet's provenance was authored by its sender. The drift it exists to catch is precise and likely: a later change that lets a caller pass provenance through again, which would silently restore the self-report this build removes and leave the dial reading green on a number nobody computed.
watchme.trigger: each read of the probe over ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets — no clock and no new firing path; it rides the shim's existing pulse and the read-side overdue() door, the same seam every other probe in the corpus sits on. TRUE when at least 15 packets have berthed UNDER THE NEW DOOR (filename stamp >= 20260814T000000) and not one of them earned 'floor' for any field.
watchme.enough: CORRECTED AT THE BUILD, and the as-cast clause is kept above rather than rewritten (Law 7). As cast it read 'ENOUGH when that fraction is measured rather than declared, i.e. when no packet's provenance was authored by its sender' — which the build made UNFALSIFIABLE by construction: validate_orient now refuses a misdeclaration outright, so no berth can carry a sender-authored label and the clause is satisfied the instant the code lands. A watch that clears on the build that arms it is the check-goes-green-at-the-moment-its-condition-is-satisfied shape. CORRECTED: enough is reached when >= 15 post-door packets have berthed AND at least one field has EARNED 'floor' — an existence claim about reuse, which is the thing the code cannot prove about itself.
watchme.carrier: cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/probes/floor_earns_its_label.py — module-level PROBE, carrying the post-door counts, the per-field tally, the derived floor fraction, and (as diagnostic data only, never a trigger) the berths whose declared label disagrees with re-derivation against TODAY's tree.
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — the finding is 'the label became honest and the floor's answer is still not reused', which is a hypothesis about why, not a fact about what.
watchme.consumer: harbor_master. It deposits and pokes and carries no authority: the back-edge that re-opens this ticket is the owner's act (Law 6). A fire means read skills/chart/SKILL.md stage 1 first — a zero here is usually the ceiling treating 'carry the floor's three fields through unchanged' as a suggestion, or packets berthing with no 'request' at all, which is the cheaper half to find and is carried in the same report.

intention: orient's floor AUTHORS the packet fields that are lookup rather than language — refs, domain, unknowns — and provenance for them stops being declared by the author and becomes DERIVED from whether the ceiling changed the floor's answer.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-14 over all 45 berthed orient packets, and the measurement is the reason this is a build and not a tidy-up: NOTHING IN THE CODE PRODUCES A PACKET FIELD. The floor (floor_facts) emits facts — components_mentioned, skills_mentioned, paths_found, paths_missing, roster_size — and the ceiling then writes all five authored fields by hand and STAMPS ITS OWN PROVENANCE. domain is labelled 'floor' in 18 of 45 packets and 14 of those floor-labelled values are over 200 characters of prose; refs is labelled 'floor' in 44 of 45 while the SELECTION was always the ceiling's. So skills/chart/dial.py reads orient at 0.40 floor, and that 0.40 is a self-report. THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is Akien's: he is deciding what to build next off that dial. A pass that reports itself 40% compiled when it is 0% compiled tells him the cheapest remaining work is elsewhere, and the staircase stalls on a number nobody computed. Under the ruling of the same day the stakes are larger than tidiness — the ceiling for the preamble is becoming Hex, and the whole point of a failover is that it DEPOSITS, so 'what did the floor already answer' has to be a fact before 'what did the ceiling have to add' can be one.
traces_to: Ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap — the build order is Akien's: 'starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now ... those can be completely deterministic. and ONCE THEY WORK we can start working on the other ones later.'
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A provenance the author stamps is an unmeasured claim wearing a measurement's name.
Law 4 — a rule enforced by physics, not policy. 'label the field honestly' is discipline; deriving the label removes the discretion.
Law 9 — red is the default, green is earned. 0.40 floor is a green the corpus never earned.

Akien's 2026-07-19 pre-build-packet paper, the staircase section: 'migrate a pass only when its deterministic version passes a check a hollow one couldn't.' A self-reported provenance is exactly the check a hollow version passes.
gates: TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND IS WHAT MAKES THE FIRST HONEST. (1) floor_packet(request, root) authors refs (paths the floor verified plus the directories of components and skills it matched), domain (the addresses and their rung on tools->machines->devices->skills, derived from where those refs actually sit), and unknowns (what the floor could NOT ground — paths claimed in the request that do not exist, slash-verbs not in the skill roster). (2) PROVENANCE FOR THOSE THREE IS DERIVED, NOT ACCEPTED: the packet door compares the ceiling's field against the floor's proposal and writes 'floor' when it survived unchanged, 'claude' when it did not. A caller-supplied provenance for those fields is refused rather than trusted. The ceiling keeps intent and scope, which need language. THE CEILING MUST STILL EXTEND unknowns — the floor's unknowns are UNGROUNDABLE REFERENCES and the ceiling's are conceptual ('whether the proof or the inspector is the shaker'); a floor that crowds out the conceptual ones has made the packet worse while making the dial look better, which is this build's own worst failure mode.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a packet is berthed whose provenance for refs/domain/unknowns was written by its sender rather than derived — the self-report restored; (2) the derived floor fraction goes UP while the packets get thinner, i.e. the ceiling stopped adding conceptual unknowns because the floor had already filled the field (the crowding-out failure, and the dial would read this as progress); (3) a floor-authored ref does not exist on disk, which the existing every_ref_exists_on_disk check must catch — a floor that invents is worse than a ceiling that invents, because it wears the provenance of a measurement; (4) domain becomes prose again by any route, since the whole point is that it is derived from where the refs sit; (5) the change lands in orient and the dial's reading for the other six nexi is left looking comparable when it is no longer measuring the same thing.
horizon: Now. It is the first rung of the build order Akien named the same day, and everything after it (constrain, then survey) inherits both halves — the second half especially, because a derived provenance built once at orient is the pattern the other two are written from, and a self-report copied forward is exactly how 'a tool holds no state' reached eight charters.
dependencies: MEASURED, not assumed: floor_facts already computes every input the three fields need — component_roster, skill_roster, path existence — so half (1) is composition, not new machinery.

The inspector already has the tooth that guards a floor-authored ref: every_ref_exists_on_disk (orient.py:169) refuses any ref the floor cannot verify. It was built for ceiling-authored refs and applies unchanged.
skills/chart/SKILL.md stage 1 must change in the same act, because it is what instructs the ceiling; leaving it telling the ceiling to author refs would make the two mouths disagree.
NOT a dependency: Hex. This build is what gives Hex something to fail over FROM, but it needs nothing from hex.local and must not wait on it.
distinctions_recorded: THE DIAL IS NOT WRONG, IT IS READING A DIFFERENT THING. skills/chart/dial.py faithfully reports the provenance labels in the packets; the defect is that the labels are authored. Nothing about the dial's own code is at fault here and it should not be 'fixed' — what changes is that the labels it reads become derived. After this lands the dial finally measures what its charter always said it measured.

'FLOOR' HAS MEANT TWO THINGS AND THIS BUILD PICKS ONE. In the berthed packets it has meant 'grounded in floor facts' — a hand wrote the prose but based it on what the floor found. This build makes it mean 'produced by the floor'. That is a narrowing, and a reader comparing pre- and post-build dial readings is comparing two different measurements; falsifier (5) is that trap.

THIS IS NOT ABOUT SPENDING FEWER TOKENS. 'The goal is not to reduce token spend for you. you are cached.' The floor authoring refs does not make orient cheaper in any way that matters; it makes the answer REUSABLE and it makes the next rung's evidence real.

CORRECTION 2026-08-14, appended not rewritten: the ticket was cast with its probe requirement in the `watchme` FIELD and no WATCHME summons in the workflow STRING, which is exactly the malformation `test_watchme_spec` exists to catch — and it caught it on the next run. The field is the spec a reader follows; the string is what the emit chokepoint walks, so a probe named only in the field is a probe nothing can refuse the absence of. The object is `orient-provenance-is-derived-not-declared`.

CORRECTION 2026-08-14 #2, appended not rewritten: the `watchme` field was cast as PROSE and the spec schema wants a list of spec OBJECTS carrying the five (trigger, enough, carrier, nexus, consumer) plus a `probe` berth — `test_watchme_spec` caught it on the same run that caught the missing summons. The as-cast prose rides inside the spec as `as_cast_verbatim`, because arming the probe FALSIFIED its `enough` clause: as written it cleared the moment the code landed (the door now refuses a self-report, so 'no packet's provenance was authored by its sender' is true by construction). That is the known shape — a check that goes green at the instant its condition is satisfied — and the corrected clause asks the question the code cannot answer about itself: has any field ever EARNED the label.
provenance: Born 2026-08-14, minutes after the ruling that set the build order, out of a measurement taken to answer 'what can we build out now'. The dial said orient was 0.40 floor; opening the packets to see WHICH fields those were is what found that the fraction was a self-report. That ordering matters: the ticket exists because someone read the values behind a number they were about to act on.

chart_notes.orient: The code is at cairn/devices/builder/machines/orient/orient.py: floor_facts (:82) emits the facts, AUTHORED_FIELDS (:69) names the five the ceiling writes, inspect_orient (:123) already checks ref existence and provenance coverage, validate_orient (:183) is the gate, write_packet (:208) is the berth. The instructing prose is skills/chart/SKILL.md stage 1. The reading instrument is skills/chart/dial.py. The evidence is 45 berthed orient packets under ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/.
chart_notes.constrain: IN: orient only. OUT: constrain and survey (they are the next two rungs and inherit the pattern, but Akien's order is one at a time and 'ONCE THEY WORK'); the other six nexi's dial readings; anything on hex.local; and any change to the dial's own code. Also OUT: widening AUTHORED_FIELDS or changing the packet schema's shape — the fields stay the five they are.
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails: berth a packet whose sender DECLARES provenance floor for a domain it wrote by hand, and require the door to refuse it or to overwrite the label with 'claude'. A hollow build passes by accepting the sender's dict, which is exactly today's behaviour. Second tooth: run floor_packet on a request naming a path that does not exist and require it to land in unknowns rather than in refs — a floor that invents a ref is the worst failure here, because it carries a measurement's provenance.

filed_edges: The same self-report exists in all six other nexi's packets and this ticket deliberately does not touch them (Akien's order is one at a time). But the dial's cross-nexus comparison becomes apples-to-oranges the moment orient lands, and nothing announces that. Either the dial grows a way to say which nexi are measured, or the reading is footnoted somewhere a reader will actually meet it.

If provenance is derived by comparing ceiling to floor, then a THIRD outcome exists that the current vocabulary cannot say: the ceiling EXTENDED the floor's answer rather than replacing it (adds a conceptual unknown to the floor's ungroundable ones). Today that collapses to 'claude' and loses the fact that the floor's part survived. Worth a value of its own once there is evidence about how often it happens — not invented before then.
